title: Conditional Enhancement of Dissipation-Induced Nonreciprocity by Quantum Squeezing
authors: B. -B. Liu, D. -Y. Wang, J. Tang, Gang Chen, H. Jing, Shi-Lei Su, F. Nori
abstract: We systematically investigate the role of squeezing in improving dissipation-induced nonreciprocal coupling mediated by a common reservoir, by incorporating a $χ^{(2)}$ nonlinearity into either the cavity mode, the reservoir, or both. Squeezing is capable of exponentially enhancing the effective coupling, but this enhancement is not universal in such a nonreciprocal interaction. Instead, it depends on the system configuration and specific parameter regimes. Specifically, the squeezing of the reservoir injects additional energy into the system via the dissipation channel, modifying the underlying dynamics in a nontrivial manner. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the proposed approach enhances the performance of the quantum battery, including stored energy, charging power, and ergotropy. We provide the corresponding analytical expressions, together with a systematic analysis of energy transport and parameter optimization. Extending the framework to optical isolation, we observe an exponentially amplified output signal. Our results open a new avenue for nonreciprocal quantum information processing and nonreciprocal quantum device design.
summary: This paper systematically explores the role of quantum squeezing in enhancing dissipation-induced nonreciprocal effects within coupled cavity systems. By analyzing both energy storage (quantum batteries) and signal isolation (optical isolators), the authors demonstrate that squeezing can exponentially boost key performance metrics. The findings establish a powerful theoretical framework for designing advanced, nonreciprocal quantum devices.
main_problem: The study investigates how quantum squeezing can be utilized to enhance nonreciprocal coupling induced by dissipation in various quantum devices.
main_result: Squeezing leads to an exponential enhancement of the effective nonreciprocal coupling, significantly boosting performance metrics like stored energy and output signal strength in both quantum batteries and optical isolators.
method: The analysis employs master equations and Quantum Langevin Equations (QLEs) to model the time evolution of system operators under nonlinear and dissipative couplings. Expectation values are calculated across multiple squeezing configurations.
model_or_system: The core model involves two coupled cavity modes interacting with a common reservoir, potentially incorporating $\chi^{(2)}$ nonlinearity. Applications include quantum batteries (energy storage) and optical isolators (unidirectional signal transmission).
key_observables: Effective Coupling (EC), Enhancement Effect (EE), stored energy ($E_b$), ergotropy ($\mathcal{E}_b$), and the output transmission coefficient ($T_{ab}$).
important_parameters: Squeezing parameter ($r$), coupling strength ($J$), detuning ($\omega_s$), and cavity decay rates ($\kappa, \Gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes applying a broad-band squeezed-vacuum field to manage noise, and often simplifies dynamics by setting certain frequency parameters (e.g., $\omega_s = 0$ in some battery contexts).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy evolution of quantum batteries under different squeezing regimes, show the enhancement factor of stored energy vs. squeezing parameter $r$, and plot the transmission coefficient spectrum for optical isolators.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates five cases of squeezing application in a coupled cavity system. It then applies this framework to analyze two key physical applications: quantum batteries (analyzing energy/ergotropy) and optical isolators (analyzing transmission coefficients).
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, quantitative methods for engineering nonreciprocity using fundamental quantum resources like squeezing, which is highly relevant for designing next-generation quantum optical components.
